A.explanation: The equation $F = ma$ gives force only when mass is constant, so it is a special case and not the general definition.

B.explanation: The product $mv$ defines linear momentum $p$, not force.

C.explanation: Newton's second law defines force as $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, the rate of change of momentum.

D.explanation: Rate of transfer of energy defines power $P = \Delta E / \Delta t$, not force.

hints: Notice the wording difference between a product such as mass times velocity and a rate of change with respect to time.
Recall Newton's second law in momentum form: force is linked to how quickly momentum $p = mv$ changes.
Check which option describes $\Delta p / \Delta t$ and which options describe momentum and power instead.
walkthrough: Identify what each option claims: A links force to $ma$, B links it to $mv$, C links it to change of momentum per unit time, D links it to energy per unit time.
State the governing rule: Newton's second law defines resultant force as the rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
Note that $F = ma$ follows from this only if mass $m$ is constant, since then $\Delta p / \Delta t = m\Delta v / \Delta t = ma$.
Eliminate B because $mv$ is momentum itself, and eliminate D because energy transferred per unit time is power.
Conclude that the general definition is the rate of change of momentum. This is option C.
